question_text: A word processing program allows the user to:
option_a: Only view documents, not edit them
option_b: Create, edit, format, store and print text documents
explanation: A word processing program allows the user to create, edit, format, store and print text documents.

question_text: According to this unit, when text does not fit on a line and automatically flows to the next line, this is called:
explanation: When text does not fit on a line, it automatically flows to the beginning of the next line -- this is called word wrap.

question_text: According to this unit, should you press [Enter] at the end of every single line of text while typing in a word processor?
option_b: No -- [Enter] is used to end a short line, end a paragraph, or create a blank line
explanation: You must not press [Enter] for every line; word wrap handles that automatically. [Enter] is used to end a short line, end a paragraph, or create a blank line.

question_text: Special symbols that indicate each time [Enter], [Spacebar], and [Tab] have been pressed are called:
explanation: Nonprinting characters are special symbols indicating where [Enter], [Spacebar], and [Tab] were pressed; they can be displayed via the Show/Hide button.

question_text: Pressing the Tab key while typing inserts a tab character, moving the insertion point to the next tab stop, which are preset at what increments?
explanation: Tab stops are preset at 1.27cm increments.

question_text: The Word feature that suggests the completion of common words, dates, or names after you type the first few letters is called:
explanation: AutoComplete suggests the complete word or phrase after typing the first few letters; press [Enter] or [F3] to accept.

question_text: Which command allows you to save a document for the first time, with a new filename, or in a different location?
explanation: The File, Save As... command enables saving a document for the first time, with a new filename, or in a different location.

question_text: By default, is Word in insert mode or overtype mode?
option_d: It depends on the document type
explanation: By default, Word is in insert mode; text to the right of the insertion point is pushed to the right as you type.

question_text: In overtype mode, what happens as you type, compared to insert mode?
option_a: Text is pushed to the right, same as insert mode
option_b: Existing text is replaced one character at a time
option_c: Nothing can be typed at all
option_d: Only bold text can be entered
explanation: Overtype mode replaces existing text one character at a time, instead of pushing text to the right as insert mode does.

question_text: According to this unit, what happens when you point anywhere inside a word and double-click the mouse button?
option_b: The word is selected, with the trailing space automatically included
option_c: The cursor moves to the beginning of the document
explanation: Double-clicking inside a word selects the word, and the trailing space is automatically selected along with it.

question_text: According to this unit's general rules, how often should you save your document while working?
option_a: Only once, at the very end
explanation: General rules for saving include: save at least once every 15 minutes, save before printing, and save before spell-checking.

question_text: Which shortcut key combination applies Bold formatting?
explanation: [Ctrl] + B applies Bold; [Ctrl] + I applies Italic; [Ctrl] + U applies Underline.

question_text: Formatting buttons like Bold, Italic, and Underline are described as being what type of button?
option_b: Toggle buttons -- the same button turns the format on and off
explanation: Some formatting buttons are toggles -- the same button is used to turn a formatting feature 'on' and 'off', e.g. bold, italic, underline.

question_text: This unit lists four paragraph alignment options. Which of the following is one of them?
explanation: The four alignment options are Left, Center, Right, and Justified.

question_text: Which alignment option is the default paragraph-alignment setting in Word, where text is aligned along the left indent with a ragged right side?
explanation: Left alignment is the default paragraph-alignment setting; the right side of the paragraph appears ragged.

question_text: According to this unit, is the spelling checker a substitute for proofreading?
option_b: No -- it is no substitute for proofreading, but can help create and edit documents
option_c: It replaces proofreading only for short documents
option_d: The unit does not address this
explanation: Although a spelling checker is no substitute for proofreading, it can be used to help create and edit documents.

question_text: A spreadsheet consists of information written in tabular form. A series of data depicted horizontally is called a:
explanation: A series of data depicted horizontally is called a 'row', while data depicted vertically is called a 'column'.

question_text: According to this unit, what is a key limitation of a 'paper spreadsheet' compared to an electronic one?
option_b: Paper spreadsheets are static -- changing one number requires manually redoing dependent calculations
option_c: Paper spreadsheets are faster to calculate
option_d: There is no difference between them
explanation: Paper spreadsheets are static; if a raw number changes, all dependent calculations must be redone manually, causing a domino effect of errors if missed.

question_text: An Excel file, which can contain multiple worksheets, is called a:
explanation: An Excel file, called a workbook, can contain worksheets. The default workbook contains 3 worksheets (Sheet1 through Sheet3).

question_text: In an Excel worksheet, the intersection of a column and a row is called a:
explanation: A cell is the intersection of a column and a row; cells are named by their column and row location, e.g. A1.

question_text: By default, how is text aligned when entered into an Excel cell?
explanation: By default, text is left aligned in the cell, while numeric entries and calculated results are right aligned.

question_text: To change an entry before it is entered into an Excel cell, which key clears the entire entry?
explanation: Pressing [Esc] (or clicking the Cancel button in the formula bar) clears the entire entry before it is entered into a cell.

question_text: In Excel, formulas are created by preceding the expression with which symbol?
explanation: In Excel, you create formulas by preceding the expression with an equal sign (=), e.g. =B1+B2.

question_text: Which symbol is used in Excel to indicate exponentiation (raising a number to a power)?
explanation: The caret (^) symbol is used to indicate exponentiation; for example, 10^2 equals 100.

question_text: Which keyboard shortcut reverses your last action in Excel (Undo)?
explanation: The speed key combination [Ctrl] + Z has the same effect as clicking the Undo button, reversing the last action.

question_text: According to this unit, applying formatting to a number in Excel (e.g. changing 10 to R10) changes:
option_a: Only the number's appearance, not its underlying value
option_b: Both the appearance and the underlying value
option_c: Only the underlying value, not the appearance
option_d: Neither the appearance nor the value
explanation: Applying a format changes only the appearance of a number, not its value.

question_text: When a column is too narrow to display a formatted number, Excel displays a series of what symbols in the cell?
explanation: When numeric data is too wide for a manually-set column width, number signs (hash symbols, #####) are displayed in the cell.

question_text: By default, are text entries and numeric entries aligned the same way in an Excel cell?
option_a: Yes, both are centered by default
option_b: No -- text is left aligned by default, while numbers/calculated results are right aligned
option_c: Yes, both are right aligned by default
explanation: By default, text entries are left aligned while numeric entries and calculated results are right aligned.

question_text: Which function key can be used to quickly create a default column chart from selected data in Excel?
explanation: Pressing [F11] after selecting a data range creates a chart using Excel's default chart format (a column chart with a legend).

question_text: A chart symbol that represents a single data point on a chart is called a:
explanation: A data marker is a chart symbol that represents a single data point, which can be displayed as a bar, column, line, pie slice, or other shape.

question_text: The vertical axis on a chart, against which values for data points are plotted, is also known as the:
explanation: The value axis is typically the vertical axis on a chart, also known as the y-axis, against which values for data points are plotted.

question_text: To create a chart from non-adjacent data on a worksheet, you select the first range, then hold which key while selecting the second range?
explanation: To select non-adjacent data, select the first range, then press the [Ctrl] key while selecting the second range, then press [F11].

question_text: A chart that is displayed on the same sheet as the worksheet data, rather than on a separate chart sheet, is called a(n):
explanation: An embedded chart is displayed on the same sheet as the worksheet, allowing you to print a chart and its data together on the same page.

question_text: According to this unit, when you change a worksheet value that a chart is based on, what happens to the chart?
option_a: Nothing -- the chart must be manually redrawn
option_b: The chart data point updates automatically, because Excel creates an active link between them
option_d: Only chart sheets update, embedded charts do not
explanation: Excel creates an active link between worksheet values and chart data points; when a worksheet value changes, the linked chart data point updates automatically.

question_text: According to this unit, how many different chart types does Excel provide via the Chart Type button drop-down menu?
explanation: A drop-down menu including buttons for 18 different chart types is displayed when you click the arrow next to the Chart Type button.

question_text: The Format Plot Area dialog box, used to format the gray background behind a chart, contains how many tabs?
explanation: The Format Plot Area dialog box contains a single tab, namely the Pattern tab, only.

question_text: PowerPoint is an application program used to create:
explanation: PowerPoint is an application program used to create presentations, delivered via slides, transparencies, or automated shows.

question_text: Which function key is used to run (start) a slide show in PowerPoint?
explanation: To run a slide show, press [F5].

question_text: To end a slide show while it is running, which key do you press?
explanation: To end a slide show, press [Esc].

question_text: PowerPoint provides five working environments/views. Which of the following is one of them?
explanation: The five views are Normal, Outline, Slide, Slide Sorter, and Slide Show.

question_text: According to the design tips in this unit, how many lines of text should a landscape-mode slide be limited to at maximum?
explanation: A slide in landscape mode should be limited to a maximum of 6 lines of text, with a maximum of 8 words per line.

question_text: The AutoShapes button in PowerPoint provides access to how many shapes?
explanation: The AutoShapes button provides access to over 150 shapes, displayed via a pop-up menu with nine choices.

question_text: The toolbar that lets you add special text effects (curved, slanted, or circular text) to a PowerPoint presentation is called the:
explanation: The WordArt toolbar lets you add special effects to text, such as circular, slanted, and curved shapes.

question_text: According to this unit, what happens when you press the [Tab] key while positioned at the beginning of a line?
option_b: The insertion point moves to the next preset tab stop, indenting the text
explanation: Pressing [Tab] inserts a tab character and moves the insertion point to the next tab stop, commonly used to indent the first line of a paragraph.

question_text: Which mouse action, according to this unit, selects an entire sentence in Word?
explanation: Holding [Ctrl] and clicking anywhere within a sentence selects the entire sentence.

question_text: Which shortcut key combination applies Underline formatting to selected text?
explanation: [Ctrl] + U applies Underline formatting to selected text.

question_text: According to this unit, which alignment centers each line of a paragraph between the left and right margins?
explanation: Center alignment centers each line of text evenly between the left and right margins.

question_text: According to this unit, pressing which key after typing an entry moves the insertion point down one cell in Excel?
explanation: Pressing [Enter] after typing an entry confirms it and moves the insertion point down to the next cell.

question_text: According to this unit, what is the fastest way to widen an Excel column just enough to fit its widest entry?
option_a: Manually typing a width value only
option_b: Double-clicking the column border, which auto-fits the column to its widest entry
option_c: There is no way to auto-fit a column
explanation: Double-clicking the right border of a column heading automatically widens the column to fit its widest entry.

question_text: According to this unit, can chart formatting (colours, fonts, borders) be changed after a chart has already been created?
option_a: No, formatting is fixed at creation
option_b: Yes -- Excel provides features to format an existing chart's appearance
option_c: Only the chart title can ever be changed
option_d: Only in chart sheets, never embedded charts
explanation: Excel provides features that allow you to format an existing chart's appearance, including colours, fonts, and borders, after creation.
